description: Hola soy Julia y soy una persona apasionada por resolver problemas complejos y analizar datos espaciales. Mi mayor fortaleza es mantener la calma bajo presión y organizar proyectos de forma eficiente. Tengo facilidad para programar en Python y procesar imágenes satelitales, transformando información científica en soluciones prácticas. Además, destaco por mi comunicación clara y mi capacidad para conectar ideas distintas, asegurando que cada paso tenga un propósito definido.
summary: Agrominis is a web application designed to help farmers and ranchers adapt to wether change through optimized crop rotation and smart grazing. Addressing the "Field Shift" challenge, our solution bridges the gap between complex satellite telemetry and daily on-the-ground agricultural decisions. By integrating NASA Earth observation data (Landsat, SMAP, and GPM) with real-world botanical and herd management metrics from southern Chile (specifically the El Refugio-Cotrilla farm), Agrominis provides an interactive map with actionable alerts. This tool is vital because it empowers local producers to maintain soil resilience, manage water stress proactively during the Spring 2026 and Summer 2027 seasons, and ensure sustainable food production in the face of shifting wether patterns.
details:
What does it do or how does it work? Agrominis is a web app that translates NASA satellite data (Landsat, SMAP, GPM) into smart grazing and crop rotation decisions. It matches real-time satellite biomass calculations with the daily nutritional demand of a cattle herd (e.g., 1,010 animals at the Cotrilla farm).

What benefits does it have? It provides direct, actionable alerts (e.g., "Delay grazing in Paddock 3") and forecasts soil moisture drops. This allows farmers to prevent overgrazing and prepare for droughts proactively.

What is the intended impact of the project? It empowers local farmers to build climate resilience, protect soil health, and sustain local food production against changing weather patterns (specifically targeting the 2026-2027 seasons).

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use? We used React, Tailwind CSS, and Base44 for the frontend. For data, we integrated Earth observation models from NASA (Landsat, SMAP, GPM) and ESA (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2).

How is your project creative? Instead of showing complex scientific charts, our algorithm translates raw aerospace telemetry into simple, plain-language instructions for farmers. We also designed a high-contrast UI specifically for outdoor readability under direct sunlight.

What factors did your team consider? We accounted for real-world farming constraints: regional cloud cover (using cloud-penetrating radar), precise herd dry-matter demands (8,868 kg/day), and the critical need for short-term, actionable plans rather than abstract, distant climate forecasts.
